system_map.overview: The system is a Continuous Architecture System (CAS) that orchestrates a pipeline of agentic steps via a central FlowRunner. It uses LLM clients, governance compliance gates, and action engines to enforce architecture rules, evolve knowledge, and maintain persistent knowledge stores.

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Central orchestrator that executes sequential steps and passes shared context.

agents.name: ComplianceEngine
agents.role: Evaluates architectural deltas against governance rules and produces compliance findings.

agents.name: GovernanceActionEngine
agents.role: Determines and executes governance actions based on registered state transitions.

agents.name: AgenticMerger
agents.role: Merges governance blocks (agent-generated or user-supplied) into a coherent configuration.

agents.name: LiteLLMClient
agents.role: Provides LLM inference via LiteLLM abstraction.

agents.name: MockLLMClient
agents.role: Provides deterministic mock LLM responses for testing and simulation.

orchestration.description: FlowRunner sequentially executes a pipeline of steps, each receiving and mutating a shared context (SteeringRuntimeIndex, CapabilitySet). Governance engines act as decision gates within the flow.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Abstract access to multiple LLM providers via LiteLLM, enabling model flexibility.

tools_and_integrations.name: MockLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provide deterministic, fast, and cost-free LLM responses for testing and offline runs.

tools_and_integrations.name: GovernanceActionService
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Executes governance actions (e.g., updates to knowledge store) as part of the workflow.

state_and_memory.description: cas-knowledge directory stores global maps, patterns, rules, signals, and narratives for long-term memory and governance.
SteeringRuntimeIndex, CapabilitySet, and ArchitecturalDelta hold transient state passed between pipeline steps.

patterns.name: Sequential Pipeline with Shared Context

tool_protocols.notes: FlowRunner likely calls tools (LLM, governance) as part of step execution.

optimisation_targets.notes: Sequential pipeline ensures deterministic order and easy debugging.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Centralised orchestration keeps control explicit and avoids hidden agent autonomy.

patterns.summary: A central orchestrator executes a linear sequence of steps, passing a mutable shared context object to each step in turn.
patterns.intent: Coordinate multi-step agent workflows without complex control flow, ensuring each step sees consistent context.
patterns.context: FlowRunner in src/cas_runner/runner.py is implemented as a class with an execute method that likely iterates over step definitions, threading a context object.
patterns.solution: Define steps with a common interface (prepare_inputs/process). FlowRunner initializes a shared context (e.g., SteeringRuntimeIndex) and passes it to each step, allowing steps to read and update state.

evidence.note: Central orchestrator class managing step sequence.
Shared context type carrying state across steps.

costs: Potential bottleneck if steps are long
Sequential execution may be slower than parallel
failure_modes: Context mutation bugs if steps interfere

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any agentic workflow that requires a controlled, linear set of operations with shared state. Ensure context schema is well-defined to avoid coupling.

patterns.name: LLM Provider Abstraction

tool_protocols.notes: LLM clients are called by orchestration and governance components.

optimisation_targets.notes: Provider abstraction allows switching between real and mock models for cost and testing efficiency.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Abstraction keeps agent logic independent of model specifics while allowing different providers.

patterns.summary: LLM interactions are abstracted behind a common client interface, allowing real (LiteLLM) and mock implementations to be used interchangeably.
patterns.intent: Decouple agent logic from specific LLM vendors and enable testing/determinism.
patterns.context: The llm module defines LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient, both presumably exposing the same interface (e.g., generate).
patterns.solution: Define a common client interface (e.g., generate(prompt) -> response). LiteLLMClient calls LiteLLM to reach multiple models; MockLLMClient returns canned responses for tests.
implementation_signals: Multiple client classes with same method signatures
Presence of mock client for tests

benefits: Cost savings via mocks in CI
costs: Potential interface mismatch if new models have unique features

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful in any agentic system that relies on LLMs; ensure interface is minimal and well-documented to support swapping.

patterns.name: Compliance Gate

tool_protocols.notes: ComplianceEngine uses internal rules evaluation, not external tools.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Impose a hard gate on changes to avoid drift.

patterns.summary: Changes are evaluated against governance rules by a dedicated compliance engine, blocking non-compliant actions.
patterns.intent: Prevent architectural changes that violate established rules.
patterns.context: ComplianceEngine is invoked during the pipeline, likely after a change is proposed, to check against cas-knowledge rules.
patterns.solution: ComplianceEngine accepts an ArchitecturalDelta and rule set, returns ComplianceFinding (pass/fail plus reasons). FlowRunner uses this to decide whether to continue.
patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any system with business rules that must be enforced on agent actions; maintain rules as data.

patterns.name: Governance Action with Transition Registry

optimisation_targets.notes: Central registry ensures transitions are deterministic and traceable.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Explicit transition registry reduces uncontrolled autonomy.

patterns.summary: Governance actions are managed via a central transition registry that defines allowed state changes and triggers execution.
patterns.intent: Provide a controlled and auditable way to execute governance actions based on system state.
patterns.context: GovernanceActionEngine uses TransitionRegistry to determine permissible transitions, then calls GovernanceActionService to act.
patterns.solution: Define a registry of transitions (from state to state with action). GovernanceActionEngine looks up the current state and triggers the appropriate action service.

costs: May be overkill for simple flows

patterns.reuse_notes: Use when agent actions are many and need to be constrained by state; model transitions as data for flexibility.

patterns.name: Agentic Output Merger

tool_protocols.notes: Probably leverages LLM to reason about merge.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Uses LLM to automate merge but with deterministic output schema.

patterns.summary: The system uses a dedicated merger to combine multiple governance blocks, using agentic reasoning to resolve conflicts.
patterns.intent: Synthesize coherent governance configuration from heterogeneous sources.
patterns.context: AgenticMerger is likely used during bootstrap or when updating governance blocks from multiple sources (e.g., user-defined and auto-generated).
patterns.solution: AgenticMerger accepts multiple block dictionaries, uses an LLM to resolve conflicts and produce a merged result, validating against schema.

costs: Need to validate merged output against schema
failure_modes: Conflict resolution may bias one source

patterns.reuse_notes: Reusable for any system that needs to merge multiple agent outputs or configs; ensure strong schema validation after merge.

patterns.name: Structured Steering Context

tool_protocols.notes: Typed models serve as data contracts for prompts and step inputs.

optimisation_targets.notes: Strong typing reduces miscommunication between steps.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Explicit data models limit ambiguity and improve predictability.

patterns.summary: Agent state is captured in structured Pydantic models (SteeringRuntimeIndex, CapabilityRecord, ArchitecturalDelta) that are passed across steps.
patterns.intent: Ensure consistent data representation for agent decisions and step handoffs.
patterns.context: Steering models define the shape of runtime index, capabilities, and deltas, used by FlowRunner and governance engines.
patterns.solution: Define typed Pydantic models with explicit fields and validation. FlowRunner passes these models as context, and steps use type hints.

failure_modes: Over-engineering if models are too rigid

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt in any multi-step agent pipeline; use Pydantic or similar for validation.

patterns.name: System Health Self-Assessment

tool_protocols.notes: Health model computes status from internal metrics.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Central health assessment helps operators, not autonomous response.

patterns.summary: The system maintains a health model that aggregates metrics to compute a health status and reasons for that status.
patterns.intent: Provide a quick summary of system health to aid monitoring and decision-making.
patterns.context: HealthModel module defines HealthStatus, calculate_health, and get_health_reasons, likely used in a dashboard or CLI.
patterns.solution: Define HealthStatus enum (e.g., healthy, degraded, unhealthy). calculate_health takes metrics and returns status; get_health_reasons provides explanation.

failure_modes: Misleading health status if metrics are wrong

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful for any agentic system needing observability; keep metric definitions configurable.

patterns.name: Workspace Bootstrap and Merge

tool_protocols.notes: Bootstrap initializes directories and merges governance blocks.

patterns.summary: The system bootstraps a workspace by merging a base governance block with user configuration and creating necessary directories.
patterns.intent: Set up a consistent project structure and governance baseline for agentic processes.
patterns.context: bootstrap.py contains bootstrap, init_workspace, and merge_cas_governance_block functions, likely called from CLI.
patterns.solution: init_workspace creates dirs; merge_cas_governance_block combines a default block with provided config; bootstrap orchestrates both.

costs: May overwrite user changes if not careful

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to tools that need standard project scaffolding with configurable governance.

patterns.name: Persistent Knowledge Store

tool_protocols.notes: Knowledge is stored in filesystem as YAML/MD, acting as a blackboard for agents.

optimisation_targets.notes: Long-term learning improves agent decisions over time.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents read from persistent store but do not own it exclusively.

patterns.summary: The system maintains a persistent knowledge base (patterns, rules, signals, narratives) that agents read and write to inform decisions.
patterns.intent: Provide long-term organisational memory that persists across runs and projects.
patterns.context: cas-knowledge directory contains global (patterns, rules, signals, maps) and project-specific (projects/) knowledge, used by governance and steering.
patterns.solution: Store knowledge in structured files (YAML/MD) under cas-knowledge. Agents (via GovernanceActionService) update these files based on learning.
patterns.reuse_notes: Use a persistent store for any agentic system that needs to learn or enforce long-lived rules; consider structuring as files or database with clear schemas.

patterns.name: Human-in-the-Loop Governance

tool_protocols.notes: Some actions require human approval before execution.

optimisation_targets.notes: Human review prevents risky autonomous decisions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Keep humans in the loop for critical governance decisions.

patterns.summary: Critical governance decisions (e.g., pattern promotion, rule updates) require human approval as part of the workflow, balancing automation with oversight.
patterns.intent: Prevent fully autonomous governance actions that could have broad impact.
patterns.context: Mentioned in governance lifecycle flows, likely implemented via GitHub workflows or manual steps that pause the pipeline.
patterns.solution: Governance lifecycle includes checkpoints where human reviewers can approve or reject automated actions, often via PR reviews or manual approvals.

evidence.note: Describes governance lifecycle with human steps.
CI/CD workflows that may include manual gates.

benefits: Reduces risk of bad autonomous decisions
failure_modes: Approval steps may be skipped or rubber-stamped

patterns.reuse_notes: For any agentic system with significant actions, build explicit human approval gates; consider using existing workflow tools (GitHub Actions) for handoffs.

patterns.name: Pattern Evolution and Promotion

tool_protocols.notes: System promotes heuristics to patterns based on evidence.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Automated detection but human approval for promotion.

patterns.summary: The system evolves its knowledge base by promoting heuristics to formal patterns based on accumulated evidence and governance review.
patterns.intent: Ensure architecture patterns are continuously validated and updated as the system learns.
patterns.context: Described in cas-pattern-evolution-flow.md; likely uses signals/heuristics to identify emerging patterns and promotes them via governance actions.
patterns.solution: Track heuristics (empirical signals) and use governance actions to promote them to patterns when evidence mounts, with human approval.
patterns.reuse_notes: Useful for systems that aim to learn from operational experience; ensure a clear promotion criteria and governance.

patterns.name: Governance Inventory and Health

tool_protocols.notes: Models capture governance health and throughput.

patterns.summary: The system models governance inventory, health, throughput, and risks to evaluate the effectiveness of its own governance mechanisms.
patterns.intent: Provide self-monitoring of governance quality to detect issues early.
patterns.context: Models like GovernanceInventory, GovernanceHealth, GovernanceThroughput, GovernanceRisks are defined, likely used by dashboard or reporting.
patterns.solution: Define Pydantic models for governance health indicators and calculate them from collected data (e.g., compliance rates, action counts).

failure_modes: Indicators may not reflect true health

patterns.reuse_notes: Use metric models to evaluate any self-regulating agentic system; ensure metrics align with actual outcomes.

anti_patterns.name: Central Orchestrator Bottleneck
symptoms: All steps must pass through FlowRunner, creating a single point of failure.
Long pipelines increase wall-clock time even for independent steps.
suggested_remediation: Introduce parallel execution for independent steps (fan-out/fan-in)
Consider an event-driven orchestration for non-linear flows

anti_patterns.name: Hidden LLM Dependency
symptoms: Agent workflows may invoke LLM calls indirectly through merged components (e.g., AgenticMerger) without explicit prompts logged.
Mock vs real LLM behaviour may diverge, causing environment-dependent results.
Lack of traces for LLM decisions makes auditing difficult.

where_observed.note: Uses LLM for merge but no explicit trace evidence

suggested_remediation: Add explicit prompt logging and trace spans (e.g., OpenTelemetry)
Implement a structured output schema for all LLM calls
Make mock client behaviour configurable and transparent

cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Strong typing ensures agents adhere to known schemas, though not all LLM calls may be fully contract-bound.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Health model and governance metrics (GovernanceHealth, GovernanceThroughput) provide periodic assessment of system state.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Self-evaluation is focused on governance effectiveness, not on LLM output quality (e.g., hallucination).

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Compliance engine and human-in-the-loop governance gates prevent unauthorized changes.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Safety is addressed through rule enforcement and human approvals, not through model-level guardrails.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Mock LLM client and LiteLLM provider abstraction enable cost-effective testing and model selection.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Abstraction allows switching to cheaper models or using mocks during CI, but no explicit budgeting mechanism.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: OpenTelemetry dependencies and governance metrics suggest tracing and health dashboards.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Observability is likely used for performance, but LLM-specific traces are not evident.
